answer: Each identity publishes its full failure history, and hiding 14 or more junk verdicts voids its standing entirely when discovered. Histories are stored in island, checked in walnut, and quartz shows each void. A farm cannot present clean aliases because the record follows the key, so laundering reputation through new keys does not work. A farm of 1335 identities would post 3272 proofs and burn roughly 35 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
